headline: South Sudan's New Reservoir Brings Farmers and Herders Together
meta_description: A UN-backed water project in Terekeka county is reducing conflict between farmers and cattle herders by providing a shared resource in drought-prone South Suda…
summary_short: A new artificial reservoir in South Sudan's Terekeka county is bringing together farming and herding communities around a shared water source, offering hope for peace.
body:
In Terekeka county, South Sudan, a sparkling artificial lake now stands as a quiet monument to cooperation. Built by the UN peacekeeping mission (UNMISS) as a quick impact project, the roughly 3,200-square-metre reservoir addresses far more than a chronic water shortage. For years, farmers and cattle keepers have clashed over scarce water and grazing land—a cycle of tension that has destroyed villages and displaced families. By positioning the reservoir carefully between farmland and grazing areas, the project offers both groups what they desperately need without forcing them to compete for the same space. The impact is already visible: new cattle camps have begun settling around the water source, and members of the displaced Wonduruba Mundari community are returning home.

What makes this project remarkable is how it emerged from genuine unity. When construction workers arrived at the site, they discovered no suitable road for heavy machinery. Rather than delay the work, farmers and herders from surrounding communities arrived together with tools to clear a pathway, energized by the prospect of a shared resource. A fortunate discovery of underground water meant the project could be completed in just one month while ensuring the water source would remain clean and sustainable even during dry seasons.

For John Kenyi, a cattle keeper and father of three, the reservoir represents something larger than infrastructure. He sees it as evidence that his community can work together toward a common future—that herders and farmers can coexist peacefully. In a region long fractured by competition over survival itself, this reservoir has become a place where cooperation is taking root. Whether it will ultimately reduce cattle-related violence remains uncertain, but the shift in how communities now gather around this shared resource speaks to something equally vital: renewed hope that Rego can once again feel like home.
quick_facts: UN peacekeeping mission built 3,200-square-metre artificial lake in Terekeka county
Reservoir completed in one month with help from local farmers and herders
Underground water source discovered, ensuring sustainable supply during dry seasons
New cattle camps settling around reservoir as displaced families return home
